title: Introduce Idempotency-Scope header and Retry-After-Range for OpenAI compat and tool-stream stability
author: Lina Chen
release_notes: Adds Idempotency-Scope and Retry-After-Range headers for clearer retry semantics; normalizes OpenAI-compatible error envelope; introduces a single-line streaming error frame with structured fields; opt-in header-driven behavior, no forced breaking changes.
description: Motivation: Clients and platform routing need a clearer, machine-readable separation between per-request idempotency and longer-lived conversation/session idempotency, and operators need a deterministic retry guidance window rather than a single Retry-After hint. This PR introduces two compatible surface changes to the OpenAI bridge and streaming runtime: 1) a new Idempotency-Scope request header (Idempotency-Scope: request|session|conversation) that disambiguates how idempotency keys are interpreted and persisted by the adapter and routing layer, and 2) a Retry-After-Range response header (Retry-After-Range: <min-seconds>,<max-seconds>) which gives callers a recommended retry window to support smarter backoff strategies and smoother autoscaling. In addition, this PR standardizes the structured error envelope returned by the OpenAI-compat shim to include {"code","message","retryable","retry_after_hint_seconds","idempotency_hint"} where applicable and adds a single-line streaming error frame format for tool/function-call streams (frame_type:error payload:<json-string>). Design summary: - Idempotency-Scope is advisory but authoritative for the OpenAI shim: when Idempotency-Scope=request the idempotency-key is treated as a single atomic request key; when session or conversation the adapter will attempt to correlate incoming keys across the session identifier (customer-provided) and preserve a scoped result lease for the configured lease TTL. The default behavior remains request-scoped for existing clients if the header is absent. - Retry-After-Range is emitted by rate-limiters and the serving runtime when we can estimate a best-case and worst-case window (e.g., 30,120). Consumers may choose any retry policy within that range; our SDKs will include an opt-in helper to adhere to the window semantics. For legacy single-value Retry-After we continue to set the header for compatibility. - Streaming errors: tool/function-call streams now emit a dedicated error frame as a single-line event to avoid protocol framing ambiguity. The frame contains the standardized envelope and, when a retry is applicable, includes retry_after_hint_seconds and idempotency_hint (e.g. "retry_after_hint_seconds":45, "idempotency_hint":"session:abcd1234" ). - OpenAI mapping: 429/503 map to code="rate_limit", 409 map to code="conflict" with retryable=false unless accompanied by a Retry-After-Range; validation errors map to code="invalid_request". Implementation notes: - OpenAI adapter: header parsing and mapping implemented under openai/adapter/headers.go, with unit tests and a small compatibility shim so missing headers fall back to prior logic. - Runtime: rate limiter updates in runtime/ratelimit/heuristic.go to compute a conservative min/max window and surface it via HTTP and internal gRPC for Dedicated/Private. - Streaming: new frame serializer in stream/frame.go and new parser in stream/parse_test.go to validate single-line JSON error frames. - SDKs: brief helpers added in redwood-sdk-python/ and redwood-sdk-typescript/ to surface Idempotency-Scope and parse Retry-After-Range; helpers are opt-in and behind a feature flag. Compatibility and rollout: - No breaking change: existing clients that do not send Idempotency-Scope continue to behave as before (request-scoped). Retry-After-Range is additive; we still emit Retry-After for single-value clients. - Feature gated: the adapter toggles for private/dedicated customers are behind feature flags; hosted rollout will start as opt-in for beta customers for two weeks then auto-toggle based on SDK opt-ins. Testing and verification: - Unit tests covering header parsing and mapping (openai adapter unit tests). - Integration tests with simulated throttling to assert Retry-After-Range values are well-formed and that SDK helpers respect the window. - Streaming e2e harness updated to assert single-line error frames are emitted and to validate idempotency_hint propagation during tool-call retries. Docs and migration guidance: - Added a concise spec doc to docs/openai-compat/idempotency-retry.md that describes header semantics, sample flows, and recommended SDK usage. - Migration notes advise clients to start adding Idempotency-Scope when they want session-level deduplication and to rely on Retry-After-Range for smarter backoff rather than tight fixed retries. Rollout checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] SDK helpers behind flag - [x] Docs update - [x] Beta rollout to 5 hosted customers - [x] Monitor telemetry for increased duplicate suppressions Risk and alternatives considered: We considered an opaque lease token approach (analogous to previous "lease" work) but chose an explicit Idempotency-Scope header to make behavior observable and debuggable across the OpenAI mapping layer and user agents. The Retry-After-Range intentionally provides a bounded window to allow servers to communicate uncertainty rather than forcing a single fixed backoff value. Summary of impact: improves client/platform behavior under rate pressure, reduces accidental duplicate tool invocations for session-level workflows, and yields better automated retry policies across SDKs and integrators.
commits_summary: feat(openai-adapter): parse Idempotency-Scope header and fallback rules
feat(runtime): compute Retry-After-Range and return alongside legacy Retry-After
fix(stream): single-line structured error frame serializer and parser
docs: add idempotency-retry spec and examples
chore(sdk): opt-in helpers for range parsing and idempotency scope
review_comments: Ava Patel: This addresses the ambiguity we saw in the payments team's incident where session-level replays caused duplicate charges. The header naming looks good but please add explicit TTL docs for session scope.
Lina Chen (author reply): Added TTL guidance in docs and clarified that TTL is policy-driven per deployment in the adapter README.

Diego Morales: Can we guarantee Retry-After-Range won't leak internal timing? Suggest rounding to seconds and capping max to a configured threshold. Also add a metrics tag for whether range was provided vs single Retry-After.
Lina Chen (author reply): We round to seconds and cap by runtime config; added metric runtime.rate_retry_range.present in metric exports. PTAL.
Marcus Nguyen: Approve after small nits on test coverage and ensuring SDK flag defaults to false. Tests look thorough.
Lina Chen: Addressed tests and defaulted flags to false; added integration scenario with simulated 429 bursts.
QA (automated): Verified stream error frames are one-line JSON events and SDK helper parses Retry-After-Range correctly.
